Hi Matt,

First of all, if you 'run the previous steps' it won't actually
calculate the values again -- it will check and see that it's already
done. So I would guess that it shouldn't cost you more than say 30
seconds to just rerun your old code unless you have a huge number of
arrays (hundreds to thousands?) to check. The results are saved on file
and the code in R is just to access it if it's already created. This is
probably the most straightforward thing to do.

You *should* be able to do this with fromName as follows (note the
syntax...):

cs <-
AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name="HapMap_CEU",tags="ACC,-XY,RMA,A+B,FLN,-XY",chipType=chipType,paths="plmData")


HOWEVER, I think there is an error in the code (I just updated from svn,
so I think I'm current). There are two locations in
fromName.AffymetrixCelSet() where '...' gets passed to subsequent
functions, so the 'paths' option is getting passed to findByName() as
well as fromFiles() so this creates an error (see below).

Moreover, I have another question about this -- I can't try it out right
now -- but if you have multiple cel sets in one folder (the chip
effects, probe affinities, residuals and weights, for example, from a
plm fit for microarrays) I don't know what it would find and return...

Best,
Elizabeth

> previous steps again. So far I have been unsuccessful in doing this
> using the AffymetrixCelSet function, and I am not even sure if this is

>
> > name <- "HapMap_CEU"
> > cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name, chipType=chipType)
> > print(cs)
> AffymetrixCelSet:
> Name: HapMap_CEU
> Tags:
> Path: rawData/HapMap_CEU/Mapping250K_Nsp
> Chip type: Mapping250K_Nsp
> Number of arrays: 90
> Names: CEU_NA06985_NSP, CEU_NA06991_NSP, ..., CEU_NA12892_NSP
> Time period: 2005-09-08 16:41:17 -- 2005-12-09 14:31:04
> Total file size: 5641.08MB
> RAM: 0.10MB

> > path <- "/home/matthew/Thesis/Rexamples/SNP_array/plmData/HapMap_CEU,ACC,-XY,RMA,A+B,FLN,-XY"
> > cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(path, chipType=chipType)

No, this is not correct. A main feature of aroma.affymetrix is that
you should not specify pathname. That is done on purpose for many
reasons, e.g. to make scripts 100% compatible on all platforms/file
systems/locations and to simplify troubleshooting and allow for more
validation.

The fromName() [alias byName()] construct takes a data set name
without paths, so in your case you would you use:

name <- "HapMap_CEU";
tags <- "ACC,-XY,RMA,A+B,FLN,-XY";
chipType <- "Mapping250K_Nsp";
csC <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name, tags=tags, chipType=chipType);
print(csC);

There are a few different flavors of this, so you can also do:

name <- "HapMap_CEU";
tags <- c("ACC", "-XY", "RMA", "A+B", "FLN, "XY");
chipType <- "Mapping250K_Nsp";
csC <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name, tags=tags, chipType=chipType);

and

fullname <- "HapMap_CEU,ACC,-XY,RMA,A+B,FLN,-XY";
chipType <- "Mapping250K_Nsp";
csC <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(fullname, chipType=chipType);

Note that there is in neither case a path specified; this works
because the code searches both rawData/ and plmData/ for the data set.
This is exactly how you defined your the first CEL set.

FYI, there are low-level constructs (e.g. fromFiles()) that allow you
to explicitly specify the path to the directory of CEL files, but that
is not part of the public API and should not be used by anyone (there
are also no promises that that function will remain the same).

Cheers

Henrik

Yes, there is a clash occurring because arguments '...' are passed to
multiple and different methods. Thanks for spotting this problem/bug.
I've fixed the problem and it will work in the next release.

> now -- but if you have multiple cel sets in one folder (the chip
> effects, probe affinities, residuals and weights, for example, from a
> plm fit for microarrays) I don't know what it would find and return...

The (static) fromFiles() method for each class (ChipEffectSet,
ResidualSet, WeightSet, ...) has a (default) filename pattern argument
that takes care of this.

Ok, my bad. Elizabeth's follow made it clear to me that you are of
course trying to setup a chip-effect data set, whereas I replied
before as you wanted to setup a probe-level data set. I blame this
one on a really bad jetlag. Here is how you setup a ChipEffectSet:

name <- "HapMap_CEU";
tags <- "ACC,-XY,RMA,A+B,FLN,-XY";
chipType <- "Mapping250K_Nsp";

ces <- ChipEffectSet$fromName(name, tags=tags, chipType=chipType,
combineAlleles=TRUE, mergeStrands=TRUE);
print(ces);

Note that the class ChipEffectSet is now used instead of
AffymetrixCelSet (the class decides where the data is to be located).
Note also that I have added arguments combineAlleles=TRUE and
mergeStrands=TRUE. You can do this if you know that the PLM were
fitted with these parameters. If not specified, aroma.affymetrix is
trying to infer this from the data itself, which takes time because it
has to load all data from one of the files. [Details: These two
arguments should ideally be stored in and then inferred from the data
file/CEL headers, but that is still on the to do list.]

The afformentioned alternatives to the above are:

name <- "HapMap_CEU";
tags <- c("ACC", "-XY", "RMA", "A+B", "FLN, "XY");
chipType <- "Mapping250K_Nsp";

ces <- ChipEffectSet$fromName(name, tags=tags, chipType=chipType,
combineAlleles=TRUE, mergeStrands=TRUE);

and

fullname <- "HapMap_CEU,ACC,-XY,RMA,A+B,FLN,-XY";
chipType <- "Mapping250K_Nsp";

ces <- ChipEffectSet$fromName(fullname, chipType=chipType,
combineAlleles=TRUE, mergeStrands=TRUE);

/Henrik

See my most recent reply to Mark. What is going on is that there is
one byName() (alias findName()) common for all AffymetrixCelSet
classes, which in turn calls findByName() which is specific to each
subclass, e.g.

> args(findByName.AffymetrixCelSet)
function (static, name, tags=NULL, chipType=NULL, paths=c("rawData",
"probeData"), ...)
NULL
> args(findByName.ChipEffectSet)
function (static, ..., paths="plmData/")
NULL

Cheers

yet another jet-lag typo by me. The class ChipEffectSet does not know
about 'mergeStrands' and 'combineAlleles', but CnChipEffectSet does.
Thus, do:

ces <- CnChipEffectSet$fromName(name, tags=tags, chipType=chipType,
combineAlleles=TRUE,
mergeStrands=TRUE);

Note the class.

Also, I've committed more patches so download those first;

library(aroma.affymetrix);
downloadPackagePatch("aroma.affymetrix");
